summary: Forest service tower, 80 ft, raised in Liberty County by January 1937; no later history or site description in sources reached.

events.note: Reported as already raised in a 17 January 1937 newspaper item, which says it was assembled on the ground some months earlier and tipped upright. The exact build date is not given.

evidence.supports: Listed as a forest lookout on the regional site
Site lists Bristol in its Florida section
Tower 80 feet high, one of two earlier towers; other at Aucilla in Madison County

evidence.quote: both of which are 80 feet high

evidence.supports: Forest service, as a trial, assembled the tower lying on its side on the ground
evidence.quote: the forest service, experimentally, assembled the 80-foot

evidence.supports: Gin pole, cables and a tractor tipped the tower upright
evidence.quote: and with the aid of a gin pole, cables, and a tractor, tipped it into place.

evidence.supports: Two reasons: danger to CCC enrollees, and safety rules for working men off the ground
evidence.quote: Because of the danger to CCC enrollees and because of certain safety regulations in regard to working men off of the ground

evidence.supports: Newport tower to be raised, would be the first 100-foot one raised
evidence.quote: The Newport tower, to be raised Monday, will be the first 100-foot one to be raised

sources.title: Bristol - FOREST LOOKOUTS
sources.publisher: FOREST LOOKOUTS (eastern US), regional lookout site

notes_for_editor: One source only: a regional lookout site that quotes a 17 January 1937 Tallahassee Democrat item (not checked against the newspaper itself). The item calls the tower 80 feet high and describes how the forest service raised it, but gives no builder agency beyond 'the forest service' (federal or state not stated), no later history and no site description. The source page's OCR text reads 'B5ristol'; the story avoids quoting that word. Two web searches (Liberty County 80-foot Forest Service history; 1937 CCC, Aucilla and Newport towers) found no other source about this tower; Florida Memory returned 403. The FFLA Florida index in the local cache has no entry for Bristol. The story is short because the evidence is short; do not pad it. Record status, staffing and access remain unknown.
